_comment: Ruleset 2 of 5 — Protect release trains.
Applies to release/**, hotfix/** and support/** — the branch families that
scripts/checks/check-branch-name.sh already treats as legitimate, and that
CONTRIBUTING.md documents as the only branches that may be cut from main
and kept alive after a merge.
WHY A SEPARATE RULESET
'Protect main' targets ~DEFAULT_BRANCH only. A release branch is the same
kind of object: it is cut once, built against for weeks, and must not move
under the feet of whoever is testing it. Force-pushing a release branch
silently changes what was shipped; deleting it takes the evidence with it.
WHY THERE ARE NO REQUIRED STATUS CHECKS HERE
Every workflow in this repository is triggered by pull requests that
target main (`pull_request: branches: [main]`). Requiring those contexts
on a pull request that targets release/1.2 would wait forever for checks
that never run — a permanently unmergeable branch. Review is required;
the build gate stays where the workflows actually run.
If release branches ever get their own CI trigger, add the contexts here
and re-run apply.sh.
Merge commits are allowed on a release branch (a backport of a fix that
must also be merged into the train), which is why required_linear_history
is not part of this ruleset. main itself is still squash-only.
name: Protect release branches
